chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who freed his female slave by manumission from the back (i.e., upon his death) during his lifetime. He said: If he wishes to sell her, he sells her service (bondage) for the duration of his life. So when he dies, the female slave is freed. And if she bears children, they are in her position (i.e., they are also freed upon his death).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a slave manumitted upon death (Mudabbah) and her children?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal status of a *Mudabbah* (slave woman manumitted upon the owner's death), establishing that the owner retains the right to sell her remaining service during his lifetime. It further stipulates that any children she bears inherit her status, ensuring their manumission upon the owner's death, a principle rooted in the concept of *Tadbir*. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the continuity of manumission rights for offspring, distinguishing it from other forms of partial freedom.
